### W-C: the client's watch over the stream (2026-10-15/16)

Branch `slice-wc`. Design: `notes/decisions.md`, "The client's watch over the stream". The goal:
the clients' closable range-watch contract `isEtcdRangeWatcher` (`cache/v3/InvEtcdTxn.lean`) at
the server's model for etcd's client's `*watcher` over etcd's Watch service through the stream
wire: `client.isEtcdRangeWatcher_of_watcher` (`client/v3/ServerWatcher.lean`), from
`watcher.Watch`'s spec; linked in `client/v3/Results.lean`: `client_watcher_rangeWatcher` (a
`*watcher` with `isClientWatcher V w`) and `client_newWatcher_rangeWatcher` (`NewWatcher(c)`'s
result), with `#print axioms` (no `sorry`). Every function of `watch.go` is proved but
`RequestProgress` (35 of 36, 662 of 690 code lines; `block_logger.go` 2 of 2): `run`'s proof
(`watchGRPCStream__run.lean`, ~2,900 lines) over the pure model of its state
(`WatchClientModel.lean`: the substream registry, resume queue, close and cancel transitions) and
the content lemmas (`WatchContent.lean`); `respc`'s close predicate is `False` (`serveWatchClient`
never closes it; `run`'s receive ignores `ok`, so a closed one would be a nil dereference).
Collections: `watch` gains the two results (57 entries), `client` the new boundary (73); the
baseline gains `context.WithCancelValCtx` and `streamKeyFromCtx` (234 axioms, 11 sorries).

- **Translated** (`client/v3.toml`): every function of `watch.go` (`streamKeyFromCtx` names only:
  grpc's metadata and `fmt.Sprintf` of a map), `block_logger.go`, `client.go`'s `isHaltErr` and
  `isUnavailableErr`; grpc's `codes.Internal` (`codes.toml`). Two Goose limitations met, each
  worked around by a "Gooseable:" commit on the etcd fork (the pin moves bc8b52a50 → 457b8d1b6 →
  071cbc38f): a field selection through a type alias (`wr.Events[...].Kv`, `clientv3.Event =
  mvccpb.Event`) and a `select` send case that does not convert its value to the channel's
  interface element type (`case reqc <- wr:`, written `watchStreamRequest(wr)`).
- **Handoff**: the two commits `457b8d1b6929551017810c3ee6197d222e89f331` and
  `071cbc38f2dde9e615210e8a71449be355a0a057` are in `/shared/etcd-grove-wc/.lake/etcd-fork`
  (branch `goose-lean-wc`, on `bc8b52a50`): the user must push them to `upamanyus/etcd` branch

  field selected through an alias translates (a one-line fix, tried locally: no other output
  changes); `selectStmt`'s send case should bind its value with `exprIntoType(c.Value,
  chanElem(...))` as `sendStmt` does, so a value sent on an interface-typed channel inside a
  `select` is converted.

  a fake `pb.WatchClient`, 5/5 and 3/3 runs crash): `etcd-watch-resume-closing-substream` (after a

  substream; no stream error needed). And a consequence of a known one,
  `etcd-txn-check-intervals-sibling` (a revision writing a key twice makes the watch deliver a put

- **The client's ghost design** (`client/v3/InvWatch.lean`): the watcher (`isClientWatcher`: its
  lock guarding the streams map, each a `isWGS`); per gRPC stream, `run` owns the stream's mutable
  fields and the sender's token; `serveWatchClient` forwards each response with its server content
  on `respc` (SPSC, `respcElem`); per substream (`WsPrm`), `run` sends on `recvc` (SPSC,
  `recvElem`: each response with the contract's facts already established, relative to `run`'s
  dispatch cursor `γhi`; the created one first, with no events, carrying `run`'s half of the
  request's `rev`; after a failed send, the goroutine's exit flag `γx` instead), `serveSubstream`
  publishes on `outc` (the contract's SPSC channel and cursor `γ.cur`) and hands what it holds to
  `run` on `closingc` with a membership token (`closingP`); `retc` (a bag) carries the channel with
  the consumer's resources (`retcP`, the contract's postcondition); the wait group is a
  thread-token protocol (`InvWatchWg.lean`, under the adequacy bound `threadBound GF ≤ 2^31`).
  The cursor argument: a substream's events are its watcher's deliveries (S3 + the created
  response's `idAssigned`), whose cumulative events are watch events of certified logs (S4) cut at
  revisions, so each response's events are above the previous response's last
  (`WatchContent.lean`); no reconnection, so no resume argument is needed.
- **Premises** (`watchConnFacts`): `noRetryableStreamErr` (no client stream error, nor `io.EOF`,
  has the gRPC code `Unavailable` or `Internal`: the codes `isHaltErr` lets `run` retry on; it
  exists because of `etcd-watch-resume-closing-substream`; under it every receive error stops
  `run`, and the reconnection — `newWatchClient` after `errc`, the resume queue,
  `waitCancelSubstreams` — is dead code in the verified behaviour, verified at its first call
  only); the watch-token supply `watchTokSupply` (`□ |==> mvcc.watchTok`: every create spends one;
  a finite budget would need the supply bounded by the number of creates, which the client cannot
  bound); S2 `srvProgressAllAnswers` (a response of id `-1` answers a progress request), S3
  `srvEventIdsAssigned` (a response with events carries an id the stream assigned to its
  watcher), S4 `srvWatchCert` (a watcher's deliveries are watch events of a certified log) — three
  facts of etcd's server the verified server does not state, the next mvcc unit's job (W-M2: S2
  and S3 are theorems now; S4 is not provable as planned here, see "W-M2"): S2 needs a
  "progress requested" fact threaded from `recvLoop` through `RequestProgressAll` →
  `progressAll` → `progressIfSync` into the channel invariant's `respOk`; S3 an invariant tying the
  channel's registered watchers to the stream's id map (or per-registration id tokens kept in
  `chanWatcher`); S4 the write-commit ghost step (the `γ.log`/`nev` lower bounds, `idxCert` of
  `ilog ++ [pend]`) moved to the seal before `notify` (`storeTxnWriteCore_seal`,
  `TxnWrite.End`): `watchableStoreTxnWrite.End` notifies before `storeTxnWrite.End` bumps
  `currentRev` (which takes `revMu` only around the bump; reads take `s.mu.RLock` and
  `revMu.RLock`, not the watchable store's lock), so a serializable read on the member may still
  answer the previous revision after the client got the event (allowed: serializable reads may be
  stale; linearizable ones wait for the apply); `srvNoDupKeys` (no revision writes a key twice:
  `etcd-txn-check-intervals-sibling`; the recipes' and the cache's transactions never do, so the
  premise is about other writers); `srvLogsSmall` (derived from `isServerRead`,
  `srvLogsSmall_of_read`); `R.γ.st = R.E.γ` (derived from `isWatchServer`,
  `watchSrvLink_of_server`); `pfx ≠ []` (the server reads an empty key as `"\x00"`); package facts
  (`eofOk`, `errorsNewOk`, `ctxErrClientAllW`, `clientWatchVars`); the registration
  `isGrpcStream … (watchUp R.γ) (watchSpec R)`, what `etcd_watch_served_etcd_chain` gives (its
  premises: the server's construction facts and `runsNoRequireLeader`).
- **Not covered**: `RequestProgress` (translated, not specified: its calls can make `run` panic,
  `etcd-watch-progress-closed-substream`; the verified watcher never sends a progress request).
- **The Open variant** (`isEtcdRangeWatcherOpen`, close predicate `False`, the recipes' premise) is
  false of etcd's client: `watch.go` closes the channel when the watch's context is done, when
  `run` stops (its context done by `Close()`, a halting stream error), when the server cancels the
  watch, on a failed create. It would hold only under premises that are not facts about the
  watcher (a context never done, no `Close`, a transport that never fails, a server that never
  cancels or refuses a create), not expressible as a persistent fact about `w`: no corollary. The
  recipes' contracts all take the Open variant (`isEtcdRecipesClient`; their waits read a closed
  channel as a release, `issues/recipes-dequeue-closed-watch.md`), so `queue_end_to_end` stays as
  it is: the closable contract gives the queue's wait path nothing; its enqueue path
  (`queue_vertical`) never needed a watcher. (Since unit W-Q, 2026-10-16: the closed-watch fix is
  folded into the verified fork, the recipes take the closable contract, the Open variant is
  deleted, and `queue_end_to_end_client` is the queue over the real watcher; see "W-Q".)
- **New axioms** (trust-boundary leaves): `streamKeyFromCtx` (grpc's metadata, `fmt.Sprintf` of a
  map), `context.WithCancelValCtx` (`context.WithCancel(&valCtx{inctx})`: Perennial specifies
  `WithCancel` of a `*cancelCtx`-chain parent only; `valCtx`'s `Done()` is never closed, so Go's
  `propagateCancel` takes its goroutine branch, which Perennial's model does not cover).

### W-M2: the server facts the watch client assumed (2026-10-16)

Branch `slice-wm2`. Design: `notes/decisions.md`, "The watch client's server facts in the mvcc
channel invariant". Of W-C's three server premises, **S2 and S3 are theorems**; **S4 is not
provable** (below) and stays a premise.

- **S2** `client.srvProgressAllAnswers_holds R : ⊢ srvProgressAllAnswers R` and **S3**
  `client.srvEventIdsAssigned_holds R : ⊢ srvEventIdsAssigned R` (`client/v3/InvWatch.lean`):
  projections of `v3rpc.mvccOk`'s new conjunct `mvccExtra γs r` (`v3rpc/InvWatchStream.lean`):
  `□ (⌜r.evs ≠ []⌝ -∗ ∃ γo γa, streamAuxIs γs (auxOf γo γa) ∗ mvcc.idAssigned γo r.id r.w) ∗
  □ (⌜r.id = W64 (-1)⌝ -∗ progQ γs)`, with `progQ γs := ∃ i, upAtW γs i .progress`. `sendLoop`
  establishes it at each receipt (`v3rpc.mvccExtra_of_recv`) from what mvcc's channel now says of
  the response (`watchRecvResult`: `chanRegFact γc r.w` and `⌜r.id = -1⌝ → progFact γc.prog`) and
  its run's `swsIs` (`γo.ids = γc.ids ∧ γo.prog = γc.prog`, `savedPropOwn γo.prog □ (progQ γs)`).
  `watchConnFacts` drops both; `run` instantiates the lemmas.
- **mvcc's channel** (`InvWatchStream.lean`/`InvWatchStore.lean`): `WatchChanNames` (moved to
  `InvWatchStream.lean`) gains `ids` (the stream's id map, `chanIdAssigned γc id w :=
  ghostMapElem γc.ids id □ w`, the same element as `idAssigned`) and `prog` (a saved proposition,
  `progFact g := ∃ Q, savedPropOwn g □ Q ∗ □ Q`). `watchChanInv` keeps `□ [∗list] w ∈ L,
  chanRegFact γc w` (every registered watcher's fixed range's id is assigned to it and is not
  `-1`) and `□ [∗list] r ∈ sent, ⌜r.id = -1⌝ → progFact γc.prog`. `WsStreamNames` gains `prog`;
  `isWatchStream` names its channel's `γc` (`γ.ids = γc.ids ∧ γ.prog = γc.prog`);
  `WatchParams.CR` takes `γc`; new field `WatchParams.OC w γc` (registered on `γc`: the store's
  `∃ γw, watcherMeta γ w γw ∗ ⌜γw.wc = γc⌝`); `watchStreamInv` keeps `P.IW w ∗ P.OC w γc` for
  every entry of the stream's map.
- **The registration callback** (`isWatchable`'s `watch`, `watchableStore.watch.spec`): the
  caller passes `Back : Loc → IProp GF` and `∀ w, ⌜w ≠ null⌝ -∗ |==> (chanIdAssigned γc id w ∗
  Back w)` (with `⌜id ≠ W64 (-1)⌝`); `watch` applies it once, under the channel invariant, as it
  registers `w`, and returns `Back w` and `P.OC w γc`. `watchStream.Watch`'s proof supplies it
  from its `idsInv` authority (`idsInv_assign`), getting back the invariant, `idAssigned`, `idTok`.
- **`watchStream.Watch` covers auto ids only**: premise `⌜0 ≤ sint.Z startRev ∧ id = W64 0⌝`; the
  `id ≠ 0` disjuncts and the `ErrWatcherDuplicateID` branch are gone. An explicit id can be one
  reused after a cancel (`issues/etcd-watch-id-reuse-stale-events.md`) and cannot be inserted in
  the channel's id map; the verified server never passes one (`watchReqOk` asks `WatchId = 0`).
  `recvLoop` adapted.
- **The progress fact**: `NewWatchStream.spec` takes `Q : IProp GF` and returns `⌜γo.ids = γc.ids
  ∧ γo.prog = γc.prog⌝ ∗ savedPropOwn γo.prog □ Q`; `watchServer.Watch` picks `Q := progQ γs`.
  `RequestProgressAll.spec` takes `progFact γ.prog`; `isWatchable`'s and `watchableStore`'s
  `progressAll` take `progFact γc.prog` and the map's watchers on `γc`; `progressIfSync`'s map
  premise gives each watcher `⌜rid = r.id⌝ ∨ progFact γw.wc.prog`; `watcher.send` takes
  `⌜wr.WatchID' = r.id⌝ ∨ progFact γw.wc.prog`. `recvLoop` makes `progFact` from the request it
  just received (`srvRecvTok_upAtW`). A saved proposition (`Perennial/Ghost/SavedProp.lean`), not
  an `IProp`-valued field: `progQ` is timeless, so the agreement's later is stripped at the
  receipt (`mvccExtra_of_recv` yields `◇`).
- **S4 is not provable, not even with a certificate issued at the seal** (the brief's design,
  not implemented; its content part is discharged in W-M2b by sealed logs, `mvcc.idxSealed`, and
  the clients' model's state and steps over them; what remains is `srvSealedReached`, below). `store.Read`'s postcondition `log₀ <+: log` (the read extends the caller's
  certificate) needs "certified ⇒ committed" (`mono_list_auth_lb_valid γ.idx.log`, under
  `revMu`), and it is what `rangeReplyOk`'s `F <+: log` rests on, **for serializable reads too**
  (the floor `F` from `floor_of_reached`, any `etcdReached lo`). With a seal certificate a watch
  event's revision would be such a floor; but `watchableStoreTxnWrite.End` notifies under the
  watchable store's `mu`, before `storeTxnWrite.End` bumps `currentRev` under `revMu`, and
  `store.Read` takes neither the watchable store's lock nor waits for the bump, so a serializable
  read on the member can answer the revision before the event's after the client got the event:
  `log₀ <+: log` would be false. (The clients' contract is fine: it gives serializable gets no
  floor, `InvEtcdTxn.lean`'s `serializable = false → lo ≤ r`; it is the server-side proof's
  statement that is stronger.) Making S4 true needs, besides the seal certificate (the `slog`
  mono list, its halves in the writer and the watchable store's lock), `store.Read` and its
  callers (`txn.Range`, `txn.Txn`, the read path) taking a *committed* certificate, `rangeReplyOk`
  without a floor for serializable reads, and a new argument for linearizable ones (a floor
  sealed before the request is committed by the time the read is served: the read index's apply
  wait, after `End`). A design decision for the user; W-C's note that the stale serializable read
  is "allowed" is right of the clients' contract, not of the server proof's `rangeReplyOk`.
- **What `watchConnFacts` still assumes** (W-M2b: `srvWatchCert` replaced by the narrower
  `srvSealedReached`): S4 `srvWatchCert`, `noRetryableStreamErr`,
  `watchTokSupply`, `srvNoDupKeys`, `srvLogsSmall`, `pfx ≠ []`, `R.γ.st = R.E.γ`, the package facts
  (`eofOk`, `errorsNewOk`, `ctxErrClientAllW`, `clientWatchVars`) and the registration.

### W-M2b: sealed logs for the watch path, the clients' model over them (2026-10-16)

Branch `slice-wm2`. Design: `notes/decisions.md`, "Sealed logs for the watch path, the clients'
model over sealed logs (unit W-M2b)". S4's *content* part is discharged; its *reachedness* part
cannot be (below) and stays a narrower premise.

- **`mvcc.idxSealed γ log`** (`storage/mvcc/InvIndex.lean`): `monoListLbOwn γ.hist (histOf log) ∗
  ⌜LogWf' log ∧ log.length < 2 ^ 63 ∧ ∀ cs ∈ log, cs.length < 2 ^ 63⌝`, persistent (timeless:
  `etcdserver/InvRequest.lean`). Lemmas: `idxCert_sealed` (a certified log is sealed),
  `idxSealed_prefix` (two sealed logs are in prefix order; `idxSealed_cmp` curried),
  `idxSealed_pure`, `idxSealed_agree_len`, `idxSealed_nil`, `IdxWf.sealed`. No lemma against the
  writer's committed log (false in the gap).
- **Where it is carried**: `idxWriter_seal`, `storeTxnWriteCore_seal`, `isTxnWriteCore_seal`
  return `idxSealed γ.idx (ilog ++ [pend])` (the pure facts from `IdxWf ilog pend`);
  `watchableStore.notify.spec`'s precondition, `evsWf` (so `chanWatcher`'s, `delivsCut`'s and the
  victims' delivery facts), `watchRecvOk` carry `idxSealed γ.st.idx L` in place of the bare
  history bound. The registration's `C` (`watchableStore__watch.lean`) and `sw_evsWf_extend`'s
  `C` are weakened with `idxCert_sealed`; `syncedBelow_of` takes the bound out of the seal.
  `watchRecvOk_cert`/`watchGuarantee_unfiltered` keep their `idxCert` statements. Reads,
  `idxCert`, `γ.log`, `store.Read`, `rangeEvents`, compaction: untouched.
- **The clients' model** (`v3rpc/ClientModel.lean`): `srvLog E log := idxSealed E.γ.idx log ∗
  ⌜LogSmall log⌝` (so `srvEtcdState`, `srvStep` over sealed logs); the laws with
  `idxSealed_cmp`/`sealed_pure` (`idxCert_pure` kept, a corollary). New `etcdState_of_sealed`,
  `etcdState_of_sealed_last`; `etcdState_of_cert(_last)` corollaries, so the read path's users
  do not change. **`srvReachedAt` stays `∃ log, idxCert E.γ.idx log ∗ ⌜sint.Z r < log.length⌝`** (until W-M3,
  which states it over `certOk` and takes the floors from the clients' updates):
  `client/v3`'s `floor_of_reached` turns `etcdReached lo` into a certified floor `F` for
  `rangeReplyOk`'s `F <+: log` (Get, Put, Delete, Txn: `ServerKV*.lean`), which `store.Read`'s
  `log₀ <+: log` gives only for a committed `F`; over sealed logs it would be false (the gap), so
  no `etcdReached_of_sealed`.
- **`storeSmall γ := □ ∀ log, mvcc.idxSealed γ.idx log -∗ ⌜txn.LogSmall log⌝`** (`InvRead.lean`;
  one revision more than before under the same justification, a bound on the store's size);
  its uses on certificates (`EtcdServer__Range`, `EtcdServer__Txn`, `etcdState_of_cert`) weaken
  with `idxCert_sealed`. `srvLogsSmall R` and `srvNoDupKeys R` (`client/v3/InvWatch.lean`)
  quantify over `idxSealed R.γ.st.idx log` (`srvLogsSmall_of_read` unchanged).
- **S4 narrowed** (discharged in W-M3): `watchRecvCert` and `srvWatchCert` are gone; the client uses `watchRecvOk`
  directly (`recv_unfiltered`, `dispatch_content`, `run`'s `cursorOk`: cuts over sealed logs).
  What remains is `srvSealedReached R := □ ∀ L j, mvcc.idxSealed R.γ.st.idx L -∗ ⌜sint.Z j <
  L.length⌝ -∗ etcdReached (EM := etcdModelOfServer R.E) j`, used once, in `ev_ok`, for
  `rangeWatchEvOk`'s `etcdReached e.rev`. It is **false in the gap** between the notify and the
  commit (as S4 was), for the same reason a seal certificate was: `etcdReached` is a floor of
  every later read, serializable ones included. Discharging it needs the server-side change W-M2
  described (committed certificates for `store.Read`, no floor for serializable range replies, a
  linearizable-read argument through the apply wait).
- **Final `watchConnFacts V`** (its `srvSealedReached` discharged in W-M3): `grpcConn` ∗
  `isGrpcStream … (watchUp V.R.γ) (watchSpec V.R)` ∗
  `watchDescOk` ∗ `watchTokSupply` ∗ `noRetryableStreamErr` ∗ `srvSealedReached` ∗ `srvLogsSmall`
  ∗ `srvNoDupKeys` ∗ `eofOk` ∗ `errorsNewOk` ∗ `ctxErrClientAllW` ∗ `clientWatchVars` ∗
  `⌜V.R.γ.st = V.R.E.γ ∧ V.pfx ≠ []⌝`. W-C's statements unchanged.
- **Outside mvcc, v3rpc, client/v3**: `etcdserver/InvRead.lean` (`storeSmall`),
  `etcdserver/InvRequest.lean` (the timeless instance), `EtcdServer__Range.lean`,
  `EtcdServer__Txn.lean`, `Spec/.../mvcc/watchableStore__notify.lean`, and in `client/v3`'s
  recipes `Vertical.lean` (`queueTaken` over sealed logs, `srvState_cert` renamed
  `srvState_sealed`: the model's state is a sealed log's) and `recipes/Results.lean` (docstring).
  Docstrings saying "certified" in `cache/v3/InvCache.lean`, `InvEtcd.lean` and `EtcdModel.lean`
  were left as they are (EtcdModel is not to change; the others would only rebuild the cache).
- **Soundness and faithfulness**: sealed logs are prefix-ordered, so the model's state per
  revision is unique and its laws hold; the model's laws are agreement, revision bounds,
  create/modrev persistence and the steps, none a floor, so nothing downstream weakens. It
  records what etcd gives: a watch event certifies the revision's *content*, not that a
  subsequent serializable read sees it (a linearizable one does, through the apply wait, a
  different fact). `idxCert` keeps meaning "committed", and the read specs keep their floors.
- **Gates**: `lake build` (with the path manifest) passes, 5,081 jobs; `etc/tcb-report.py --check`:
  the trust base matches the baseline (229 axioms, 12 sorries; S4 was a premise inside a
  definition, so no diff); every collection `--check --update`: no change; `etc/gen-link.py` in
  every mode and `etc/gen-btree-link.py` reproduce every `Link.lean` (the `raft` mode included);
  `etc/goose.py --check --src etcd=/shared/etcd-grove/.lake/etcd-fork`: the five projects up to
  date; `etc/verified-code.py --reuse`: unchanged (raft 257 of 327, etcd 995 of 3,599, register 25
  of 33, porcupine 25 of 45, lintest 7 of 8).

### W-M3: S4 a theorem; floors from the committed KV state (2026-10-16)

Branch `slice-wm3`. Design: `notes/decisions.md`, "`etcdReached` as a committed KV certificate;
floors from the committed state (unit W-M3)". **S4 is a theorem**: `srvSealedReached` is gone,
and no premise replaces it.

- **What the watch events carry** (`storage/mvcc`): `mvcc.evLog γ L := idxSealed γ.idx L ∗
  certOk γ L` (`InvWatchStore.lean`; `evLog_sealed`, `evLog_certOk`, `evLog_of_cert`,
  `evLog_cmp`, `evLog_nil`). `evsWf` (so `chanWatcher`'s, `delivsCut`'s and the victims'
  delivery facts), `watchableStore.notify.spec`'s precondition and `watchRecvOk` carry
  `evLog γ.st L` in place of W-M2b's `idxSealed γ.st.idx L`. `watchableStoreTxnWrite.End` passes
  `certOk γ.st (ilog ++ [pend])` from its `certOkNext` (`pend ≠ []` in the notifying branch);
  `syncWatchers` (`sw_evsWf_extend`) takes the committed log's `certOk` from `revMuInv` with its
  `idxCert`; a registration's empty deliveries are over the empty log (`evLog_nil`). Reads,
  `idxCert`, `idxSealed` and every mvcc floor are untouched.
- **`srvReachedAt E r := ∃ log, certOk E.γ log ∗ ⌜sint.Z r < log.length⌝`**
  (`v3rpc/ClientModel.lean`; timeless; `EtcdModel` unchanged). `etcdReached_of_cert` is replaced
  by `etcdReached_of_certOk`; every reply carries `certOk` of its log: `rangeReadOk`/`txnReadOk`
  (`store.Read`'s, threaded through `txn.Txn.specRead`), the writes' `appliedOk`/`resultIsW`
  (the apply thread's `kvCert` of the log after, `kvCert_certOk`), and on up through v3rpc
  (`rangeAnsOk`, `txnReadAns`, `putApplied`, `deleteApplied`, `txnAppliedAns`) to the client
  (`rangeReplyOk`, `putReplyOk`/`putReplied`, `deleteReplyOk`/`deleteReplied`, `txnReplied`).
- **The writes' results are tied to the log the write met**: `resultIsW`, `appliedOk` and
  `entryWit` take the log `lb` the entry met (`y.log`/`x.log`); the apply thread builds `entryWit`
  at the entry's position after its applied raft log `A` (`kvApplied_log`: `x.log = kvModel A`);
  `processInternalRaftRequestOnce`/`raftRequest` return `∃ L, srvRLogLb L ∗ ⌜kvModel ρ.kv L = lb⌝ ∗
  □ Qr L`; so `EtcdServer.Put`/`DeleteRange` give `□ Q (kvStateOf x.log)` (was `∃ σ, □ Q σ`) and
  `txnAppliedOk` carries it: the state the update linearized at is the state of the log the write
  met (T2's "refinement for the next unit").
- **A read-only `Txn` takes a read deposit, as `Range`**: `EtcdServer.Txn.spec` gains `Qr`
  (`kvDep γr.kv Qr` when read-only; the read loop's `readServed_logR` and `readWit_fire` as
  `Range`'s), `txnReadOk`/`txnReadAns` carry the deposit's result at a committed raft log whose
  model is the log read, `kvDepPre`'s transaction case admits a read deposit for a linearizable
  read-only transaction, and `etcdTxnSpec` a `kvReadAu` (at the read names) for one.
- **The floors** (`client/v3/InvServerKV.lean`). The mechanism is the client's, not the KV ghost
  state's (the brief's recommended snapshot inside `etcdKV` was not needed): a client holding
  `etcdKV` keeps it in `kvClientInv γ γm := inv kvClientN (∃ σ, etcdKV γ.kv σ ∗ monoNatAuthOwn γm 1
  σ.rev)`; `kv_cert_floor` (`etcdserver/KVApply.lean`) shows, with `kvInv`, `kvCertInv` and
  `srvRaftLogInv` (opened inside the client's invariant), that `etcdKV σ` and `certOk l` give
  `l.length ≤ σ.rev + 1` (the committed state's log extends every certified log, `kv_cert_read`
  and `srvRLog_lb`); `kv_client_floor` turns it into a lower bound of the counter; every update
  moves the counter (`kvOpStep_rev`). So **`kvAnyAu E γ := □ ∀ op l, certOk E.γ l ={⊤}=∗ kvOpAu
  γ.kv op (fun σ => ⌜l.length ≤ σ.rev + 1⌝)`** (`kvAnyAu_of_inv`: from `srvKVInvs E γ` and
  `kvClientInv γ γm`). `floor_of_reached` is replaced by `certOk_of_reached` (`etcdReached lo` is a
  certified log longer than `lo`) and `floor0_of_read` (the specs' mvcc floor `F` is the read
  side's first certificate). A linearizable get's floor is its read update's result at
  `kvStateOf log` (`rangeReplyOk`); a put's, delete's or writing transaction's its update's at
  `kvStateOf x.log`; a linearizable read-only transaction's its read update's; a serializable read
  has none (`kvGetResult`, `txnCommitResult`, `readTxnResult` ask none). The specs' `F <+: log`
  conjuncts are kept (an mvcc fact, with `F` the first certificate in the derivations; a caller
  holding another `idxCert F` still gets it, `client_get_after_put`).
- **Statements that changed form**: the server's specs `EtcdServer.{Put,DeleteRange}` (`certOk` of
  the log after, `□ Q (kvStateOf x.log)`), `EtcdServer.Txn` (`Qr`, read deposit),
  `EtcdServer.{processInternalRaftRequestOnce,raftRequest}` (`lb`), `txn.Txn.specRead` (`certOk`),
  `watchableStore.notify` (`evLog`); the v3rpc answers above and `put_end_to_end`,
  `deleteRange_end_to_end`, `txn_end_to_end` (`∃ σ, □ opDepQ d σ` folded into the answers),
  `etcdReached_of_hdr`, `revToken_of_put`, `etcdState_of_txnRead`; etcdserver `txn_readonly`,
  `txn_applied`; the client's `etcdPutSpec`, `etcdDeleteSpec`, `etcdTxnSpec` (the `□ Q` in
  `putReplied`/`deleteReplied`/`txnReplied`, which take `Q`), `client_put_end_to_end`,
  `client_delete_end_to_end`, `client_txn_end_to_end` (posts: `…Replied … Q …` in place of
  `…Replied … ∗ ∃ σ, □ Q σ`), `putReplied_ok`/`deleteReplied_ok`; `kvAnyAu` (the `E` argument and
  the floor), `kvAnyAu_of_inv`, `kvWritesOk` (adds `kvAnyAu E γr`), `isEtcdKVTodo_of_kv` (adds
  `kvAnyAu E γr`), `isEtcdTxnKVTodo_of_kv` (adds `kvAnyAu E γr`), `kv_txn_commit`,
  `putResult_of_reply`/`deleteResult_of_reply`/`txnCommitResultTok_of_reply` (the update's floor
  in place of `F`'s), and `kvLeasedCommitTodo` (a premise: now in the clients' model, as
  `kvLeasedPutTodo`: `txnCommitResultTok` from `etcdReached lo`, and `txnAnyResult`; a writing
  transaction with a lease has no update to take its floor from). `client_watcher_rangeWatcher`,
  `client_newWatcher_rangeWatcher`, the recipes' results and `queue_vertical*` keep their form.
- **Final `watchConnFacts V`**: `grpcConn` ∗ `isGrpcStream … (watchUp V.R.γ) (watchSpec V.R)` ∗
  `watchDescOk` ∗ `watchTokSupply` ∗ `noRetryableStreamErr` ∗ `srvLogsSmall` ∗ `srvNoDupKeys` ∗
  `eofOk` ∗ `errorsNewOk` ∗ `ctxErrClientAllW` ∗ `clientWatchVars` ∗
  `⌜V.R.γ.st = V.R.E.γ ∧ V.pfx ≠ []⌝`. S2, S3 and S4 are theorems.
- **Soundness.** `etcdReached r` now means: revision `r` is in the KV model of a committed raft
  prefix. A watch event has it at delivery (the apply thread certified the entry's model before
  applying it, and `End` hands the certificate to `notify`); a reply has it (the log read or
  written is committed and applied). A linearizable read linearizes at the committed KV state,
  which extends every certified log, so its revision is at least any `etcdReached` the caller
  holds: the floor the clients' model promises, and nothing more. A serializable read's floor is
  an mvcc fact about committed mvcc logs, kept where it was, from an `idxCert` the caller holds.
  The window between notify and commit, in which a serializable read on the member may miss an
  event it has just delivered, is etcd's documented staleness of serializable reads; not an
  `issues/` item.
- **Outside `storage/mvcc`, `etcdserver`, `v3rpc` and `client/v3`**: nothing (the `Spec/` files
  touched are of those packages: `storage/mvcc/watchableStore__notify`, `etcdserver/EtcdServer__*`,
  `etcdserver/txn/Txn`).
- **Gates**: `lake build` (with the path manifest) passes, 5,083 jobs; `etc/tcb-report.py --check`:
  the trust base matches the baseline (229 axioms, 12 sorries; no diff); every collection
  `--check --update`: no change; `etc/gen-link.py` in every mode and `etc/gen-btree-link.py`
  reproduce every `Link.lean`; `etc/goose.py --check --src etcd=/shared/etcd-grove/.lake/etcd-fork`:
  the five projects up to date; `etc/verified-code.py --reuse`: unchanged (raft 257 of 327, etcd 995
  of 3,599, register 25 of 33, porcupine 25 of 45, lintest 7 of 8).

### W-Q: the recipes over the closable watch contract (2026-10-16)

Branch `slice-wq`. Design: `notes/decisions.md`, "The recipes are verified against the
closed-watch fix (unit W-Q, 2026-10-16 · adopted)".

- **The decision.** The user folded the recipes' closed-watch fix into the verified fork, as the
  cache's `cache-ready-after-retry` before it (a bug fix, so allowed by "No code changes unless a
  bug"): fork commit `0aa6c6af8` (branch `recipes-closed-watch-channel`) cherry-picked onto
  `goose-lean` as `0df483bee`, the etcd pin of `etc/goose.py` (the translation changes only in
  `Code/go_etcd_io/etcd/client/v3/experimental/recipes.lean`: `ErrWatchClosed`, `waitEvents`
  returning a pair, its `wresp` heap-allocated per iteration). `issues/recipes-dequeue-closed-watch.md`
  and `issues/recipes-barrier-wait-closed-watch.md` are marked fixed in the verified fork.
- **Specs.** `waitEvents.spec` is over the closable channel (`isSpsc … (fun _ => iprop(True))`),
  takes the package's `isPkgInit`, and returns `(⌜err = nil⌝ ∗ waitedEvent pfx o rev typ ev ∗ ∃ rcv',
  spscConsumer γ.spsc rcv') ∨ ⌜err ≠ nil ∧ ev = null⌝`: a response whose `Err()` is non-nil
  (`WatchResponse.Err`'s spec, its precondition `statusErrOk` from `rangeWatchElem`) returns that
  error before its events are read; a close returns `ErrWatchClosed` (read from `recipesInit`,
  which gains it as a fifth fixed non-nil error); the consumer token comes back only on success
  (a close consumes it). `WaitEvents.spec`/`WaitPrefixEvents.spec`: `(⌜err = nil⌝ ∗ waitedEvent …)
  ∨ ⌜err ≠ nil⌝`. The proof of `waitEvents` links `WatchResponse.Err` and its callees in the

### W-K: the cache over the real watcher (2026-10-16, in progress; plan)

Branch `slice-wk` (worktree `/shared/etcd-grove-wq`). Goal: `cache_end_to_end_client`, the cache's
`New` over etcd's client (`isEtcdClient` derived, as `isEtcdRecipesClient_of_kv` for the recipes).
The cache's linearizable `Get` (`waitTillRevision`) makes its progress requestor call the client's
`RequestProgress`, which can make `run` panic (`issues/etcd-watch-progress-closed-substream.md`):
by the user's decision the fix is folded into the verified fork, as W-Q's. Stages:

- **K0 (the fork fix; done).** `run`'s `Canceled` case drops the substream from `substreams` after
  closing its `recvc`, so no substream in `substreams` has a closed `recvc` and the broadcast never
  sends on one: fork commit `1ac646214` (signed off as `57d502f38`; branch `watch-progress-closed-substream`, on upstream
  `f061acd09`; with the regression test `TestWatchProgressBroadcastAfterServerCancel`, which
  panics on every run without the fix; the issue's 3000-trial reproduction no longer panics),
  cherry-picked onto `goose-lean` as `107edf7e4` (both branches pushed), the etcd pin; the translation changes only
  in `watchGRPCStream.run`. `run`'s proof follows the fixed code: the model (`WatchClientModel.lean`)
  gains `CI` (the ids of the substreams `run` closed on a server cancel; ghost, so no two share an
  id), `closedRun X` is out of `substreams` (`M !! X = none`, in no entry of `M`, `CI !! X = some
  ws`), `cancelAns` moves the entry from `M` to `CI`, `closeWs` deletes from both; a mvcc response
  of a live id cannot meet a `closedRun` substream (its id is not live). No statement outside the
  model changed. Gates: `lake build` 5,083 jobs; trust base (229 axioms, 12 sorries) and every
  collection unchanged; every `Link.lean` reproduced; `etc/goose.py --check --src
  etcd=/shared/etcd-goose-lean-wk` up to date.
- **K1a (committed ≤ notified, under `s.mu`; done).** The committed log's authority
  (`idxLogAuth`) is split by the store's mode `γ.watchQ` (a new `StoreNames` field, chosen by
  `NewStore`'s caller): a plain store's (`watchQ = false`: the txn layer's `isKV`, `NewStore_backend`,
  the `writeView`s) keeps `s.revMu`'s half; a watchable store's (`newWatchableStore`,
  `isWatchableStore`'s `γ.st.watchQ = true`) gives `s.revMu` a quarter (`revQ`) and `s.mu`'s body
  the outer quarter at the notified log (`watchStoreBody`'s `"Hwlog"` is now `wlogQ γ q σ.Lmu`: the
  `wlog` half and the quarter), which the write `End` takes and gives back at the commit
  (`logQPre`/`logQPost` in `txnEndPre`/`txnEndPost` and `storeTxnWrite.End.spec`;
  `revQ_commit_pre`/`_post`; `body_commit` lends it around the inner `End`). So
  `wlogQ_cert_prefix`: under `s.mu`, every certified log is a prefix of `Lmu`. Statements that
  changed form: `NewStore.spec` (`wq`, `γ.watchQ = wq`, the quarter when `wq`),
  `NewStore_backend` (`γ.watchQ = false`), `storeTxnWrite.End.spec`, `txnEndPre`, `txnEndPost`,
  `writeView.{Put,DeleteRange}.spec` (`γ.watchQ = false`), `txn.isKV` (`γ.watchQ = false`),
  `isWatchableStore`, `watchStoreBody`, `body_commit`. Gates: `lake build` 5,104 jobs; trust base and
  every collection unchanged; every `Link.lean` reproduced.
- **A race found while designing K1b** (`issues/etcd-watch-progress-before-created.md`, reproduced
  by an integration test on upstream `main`, a hit within a few hundred trials). The server's
  `recvLoop` answers a progress request by putting the `-1` response on the watch channel, and a
  later create's `Created` on the control channel; `sendLoop` selects between them, so `Created(X)`
  can reach the client before the earlier progress response, which the client then broadcasts to
  X: for a watch X from an old revision, "nothing changed up to `p`" before X's events below `p`.
  A broadcast progress response's coverage cannot be promised to every live watch without a fix;
  a per-watcher progress response's can. The user's decision: fix it in the fork. A client-side
  fix is impossible (a progress request has no id and the server may not answer it, so the client
  cannot tell which request a broadcast answers); the server-side fix `c267e0ffe` (branch
  `watch-progress-before-created`), cherry-picked as `goose-lean` `09669450f`: `sendLoop` sends the
  responses queued on the watch channel before a `Created` response. **Done** (the pin `09669450f`,
  pushed):
  `serverWatchStream.sendLoop`'s proof over the fix, with no statement changed. The closure is
  inlined (`wp_auto`); the watch case's proof is the local macro `watch_resp k` (its four exits
  re-establish the loop invariant through the caller's `k`: the main loop's `rcv, cs, D`, the
  drain's `rcv, D, drained`), used by the `watchStream.Chan()` case and by the drain, whose
  receive is a non-blocking `select` (`blocking_rcv_implies_nonblocking` of `mvcc.watch_recv_au`);
  the control case's tail is the macro `ctrl_rest`, used with and without the drain. Gates:
  `lake build` 5,104 jobs; trust base and every collection unchanged; every `Link.lean`
  reproduced. **Next**: the ordering fact K1b needs (a `Created` at down position `j` follows every watch-channel
  response queued before it: the control response carries a lower bound of the watch channel's
  sent list, and the drain's empty receive gives received = sent: Perennial's
  `wp_select_nonblocking_alt`/`nonblockingRecvAuAlt` give the not-ready branch inside the
  channel's atomic update, so the empty buffer is observable). Perennial limitation noted:
  `wp_Len` relates a channel's length to nothing (`ChanAuSend.lean`), so a bounded drain is not
  provable; the fix drains until empty instead.
- **O1–O3 (the ordering the `sendLoop` fix gives; done).** A registered `Created` response sent at
  down position `j` follows every response of id `-1` queued on the stream's channel before it:
  - **O1 (mvcc)**: the channel's sent list is a monotone ghost (`WatchChanNames.sentl`, its
    authority in `watchChanInv`, extended by `watcher.send`); `chanSentLb` (a snapshot),
    `chan_sent_snapshot`, `watch_sent_received`, and `watch_tryrecv_au_alt` (Perennial's
    `nonblockingRecvAuAlt` for the channel: its not-ready branch, the buffer empty, gives
    `received = sent`, so `l0 <+: received` for any earlier snapshot `l0` and `chanSentLb γc
    received`; for a buffered channel, `0 < γc.ch.chanCap`, now in `NewWatchStream`'s post and
    `swsIs`).
  - **O2 (`recvLoop`)**: `WsStreamNames.sentl` (= the channel's, so the stream's names name the
    channel's order: `streamSentLb`, `chanSentLb_stream`); `ctrlWatcher`'s created case carries a
    snapshot taken after `watchStream.Watch` registered the watcher.
  - **O3 (`sendLoop`)**: the drain before a `Created` (macro `drain_created`) uses
    `wp_select_nonblocking_alt` (the whole context as `P`, by `iNamedAccu`) and
    `watch_tryrecv_au_alt`; its invariant keeps `dr = true → l0 <+: rcv` and the snapshot of
    `rcv`. `watchDn`'s control branch gains `createdAfter γs j m`: the created response's watcher
    (`idAssigned`), its `ctrlWatcher` snapshot `l0`, a later snapshot `l` (`l0 <+: l`) and the
    down list before `j`, in which every response of id `-1` in `l` is (`v3rpc.neg1_sent`,
    `sendSt_neg1`: the send loop never buffers one). Its force comes with K1b, which adds that
    the watcher was registered before `l0`. Statements that changed form: `watchDn`,
    `ctrlWatcher`, `NewWatchStream.spec`, `isWatchStream`, `swsIs`, `auxOf`.
- **K1b (mvcc: what a progress response covers; in progress).** The design is
  `notes/decisions.md`, "What a progress response covers". Done:
  - **K1b-1**: a watcher's registration index on its channel (`WatchChanNames.regi`,
    `chanRegAt γc w n`, `n` the sent length at the registration; `sentAuth` keeps the authority
    with the sent list's; `watcherIs` carries it).
  - **K1b-2a (coverage)**: `RespM.cov`, the watchers a response covers; `sentAuth` keeps
    `respCov` of every response sent (each covered watcher's responses before it are its
    deliveries, whose events are its range's up past the response's revision: `covFact`).
    `watcher.send` takes `covPre` (persistent: an events lower bound and `evsWf`; `cov_one`
    agrees it with the channel's entry, `watchEvents_cover`); `progressIfSync` covers every
    watcher of its map (all synced: `synced_d`, K1a's `wlogQ_cert_prefix`), so `progress(w)`
    covers `w` and `progressAll` the stream's map.
  - **K1b-2b (completeness of id `-1`)**: `RespM.regs` (the channel's registered watchers when
    sent), `regsOk` (a `-1` response sent at or after a watcher's registration lists it:
    `sentAuth_reg_regs`), `respCompl` (each of `regs` covered or cancelled for its reason, `rsnW`:
    its id has `rsnFor γc.rsn`, a saved predicate the stream's creator fixes: v3rpc's `cancelQ`,
    the client sent a cancel request for the id). `watcher.send` and `progressIfSync` take a
    caller's resource `CS` (lent, returned) with a persistent extraction (`complW`, `complWS`), so
    the stream's close right comes back; `progressAll` is lent `progCompl` (its branch a Boolean
    parameter, for the same reason). The stream's invariant keeps each entry's range id and, for a
    watcher out of the map, its reason (`cancelledFor`); `Cancel id` takes `rsnFor γ.rsn id`;
    once closed, every watcher of the map is cancelled. The store's `IW` says the id is not `-1`.
    Statements that changed form: `watcher.send`, `progressIfSync`, `progressAll` (and the
    `isWatchable` interface's), `watchStream.Cancel`, `NewWatchStream` (`Ψ`), `storeWatchParams`,
    `watchStreamInv`, `isWatchStream`, `swsIs`, `auxOf`, `watcherIs`. Gates so far: `lake build`
    5,104 jobs.
  - **K1b-3a**: a receipt (`watchRecvResult`) carries the response's `respCov` (against the
    responses received before it) and `regsAt` (persistent: given a watcher's registration

    channel (`P.OC`, `γ.regi = γc.regi`); `recvLoop` takes the `Created`'s snapshot after the
    registration with the index below it (`chan_sent_snapshot_reg`); `ctrlWatcher` and

  - **K1b-3b**: `RespM.idx` (ghost: the response's position in the sent list, kept by `sentAuth`,

    response and its position. `rcvOk` (now over the channel `γc`) keeps, per received response,
    `respCov`, `regsAt`, the snapshot and the position; `mvccOk` gains `mvccCov` (the channel, its
    `regi`/`rsn`/`sentl` named by the run's stream `γo`, the responses `pre` before it, the
    snapshot `pre ++ [r]`, `respCov`, `regsAt`) and that no earlier down came from the same
    response (`src_fresh`, `pend_not_sent`: the indices sent and buffered are disjoint). K1b's
    server side is complete. Statements that changed form: `RespM`, `sentAuth`,
    `watchRecvResult`, `mvccOk`, `rcvOk`.
  - **K2a (server exports)**: an event-less response covers its watcher (`respCov`'s third part:
    `watcher.send` takes it; moveVictims covers an empty batch's own watcher); `mvccCov` carries the
    saved cancellation reason (`cancelQ` at `γo.rsn`); a `-1` response has no events and a revision
    at least `1` (`respCompl`; `isStore` keeps the initial log's certificate `[[], []]`, so
    `watchableStore.rev` returns a log of length at least 2), so the client broadcasts it.
  - **K2b (the client sends progress requests and broadcasts; weak content)**: the model allows
    progress requests and `-1` responses (`progress_ok`); `reqP` admits a `*progressRequest`;
    `run`'s progress-request case sends it; a `-1` response is broadcast to every registered
    substream (`bcast_pre`, `bcast_elem`; `MapSplit.lean`: `bigSepM_split_inj`/`join_inj` split
    `run`'s substreams along `substreams`, `bigSepM_choice_inj` gives `dispatchEvent` its
    functions); `dispatchEvent` returns `true` for a broadcast. The content is still the weak one
    (no events, the cursor as it was).
  - **K2c (done)**: `wsElem` carries `noCancelOk`: for a registered substream of id X, no cancel
    request for X was sent, or its goroutine stopped (`γx`). `run` cancels a registered id only
    after a dispatch to it failed (`post_gx` keeps the stop `sendFail` publishes; the failed
    substream's element is folded back after the cancel); a fresh id has no cancel (a cancel's id
    is registered). `wsElem_mono` takes the new request list's cancels (`cancels_of_snoc`,
    `create_or`).
  - **No resume**: `run`'s `errc` case is refuted by the transport premise
    `noRetryableStreamErr` (`watchConnFacts`), so a watch never moves to another gRPC stream;
    completeness is per stream (`serveSubstream`'s resume revision is never used).
  - **K2e-1 (done)**: under `s.mu` a progress response's revision is the notified log's last:
    `store.Read` takes an optional lent fraction of the committed log's authority (`logLent`)
    and says its log is that one; `watchableStore.rev` passes it; `progressIfSync` lends its lock
    body's (`Clog = σ.Lmu`).
  - **K2e-2 (done)**: the notified log `γ.wlog` is a mono list (`notifiedLb`, `wlogQ_lb`,
    `wlogQ_lb_valid`); `End`'s commit extends it.
  - **K2e-3 (done)**: `s.mu`'s invariant is *settled* (`WsState.settled`, in `watchStoreInv`, not
    `WsOk`): every synced watcher delivered at most up to the notified log (or its first revision),
    every victim's `minRev`, in a batch or out with the mover (`Wo`), at most the notified log's
    length. Not a `WsOk` field: inside `End`'s critical section `notify` delivers the next revision
    before the commit; `notify`'s spec says both hold at `N + 1` after it. The `Wo` bound is what
    lets `moveVictims` move a victim back to synced within it (the mover's batch needs no ghost);
    the monotone `γ.wlog` (K2e-2) is not used by it, kept for (c) below.
  - **K2e-4 (done)**: `covFact` says the covered watcher's deliveries stop at the response's
    revision (`d ≤ p + 1`, or none: `d ≤ lo`). `send` is lent a fraction of each covered watcher's
    delivered-events authority (`covAuth`), so in `cov_one` the channel's events are the sender's;
    `progressIfSync` lends them from the lock's shares (`members_lend`, the map's watchers
    deduplicated). Item (b) below is done; (c) remains.
  - **K2e-5 (done)**: a pending victim batch has events (so only `progressIfSync` sends an
    event-less response), and each sent response's `respCov` has `respRev`: an event-less one's
    revision is a notified log's last and at least every earlier event-less response's on the
    channel (`send` lent the lock's fraction of the notified log, `notifiedLent`). Item (c) below:
    the earlier progress revisions are done; the start revision remains (the cache's watch starts
    at a revision etcd had reached).
  - **The start revision (2026-10-17)**: the cache's position before its first progress
    notification is its watch's start minus one, read from etcd (`Get`), so it is at or below the
    first progress revision only if the watch's server had reached it when the watch registered.
    *Route 1* (is there a bug?): with a member that lags behind the one the cache read, yes, a
    minor one: a fresh demux (`maxRev = 0`) accepts a progress below its start, and a cache watch
    "from now" is then compacted (`issues/cache-stale-progress-compacts-newest-watch.md`,
    reproduced at the demux level). The cache's contract is kept (`c ≤ p`), no fork change.
    *Route 2* (the proof, one server): carry the start's reachedness from the cache to mvcc's
    registration. Plan: (1) mvcc: `watch` takes an optional premise that the start revision is
    reached (a log below the store's: `idxCert`, or the notified log's lower bound); at
    registration (under `s.mu`, the committed log the notified one) the watcher's first revision
    is then at most the notified log's length, recorded with a `notifiedLb`; `cov_one` (lent the
    notified log, K2e-5) turns it into `lo ≤ p + 1`, so a covered watcher's `d = p + 1`. (2) The
    server's "etcd reached `r`" (`srvReachedAt`, now a raft-side `certOk`, which runs ahead of
    mvcc's commit) gains an mvcc-side lower bound: a KV reply's committed log (`idxCert`), a watch
    event's log (sealed before the notified log reaches it: the notified log must then advance at
    the seal, `End`, with a second log in the lock's state equal to the notified one when `s.mu`
    is free), a progress response's notified log. (3) The client's `Watch` takes
    `etcdReached (rev - 1)` and the watch request carries it through the stream to `v3rpc`'s
    `recvLoop` and mvcc's `Watch`. (4) The client's second cursor starts at `rev - 1`.
  - **K2e next (decided 2026-10-17: a second cursor)**: the client's channel element gains a
    completeness part with its own cursor (moved by progress responses); `rangeWatchRespOk` and
    its consumers stay. What the cache's progress case needs (`watchRespOk`: `EtcdStep c p pfx []`
    with `c ≤ p`), from the server, per covered watcher: (a) every event of its range up to `p`
    delivered before (`covFact` has it: `d ≥ p + 1`); (b) every event delivered before at or below
    `p`. (b) is not in `covFact`: `cov_one` combines the sender's delivered events (a lower bound
    `Hlb`, `d ≤ p + 1` by K2e-3) with the channel's (its half of `γw.evs`), which only contain
    them. The two are equal while the sender holds its fraction of the lock's half (nobody can
    extend `γw.evs` without both halves), so the plan is to lend those fractions to `send` with
    the coverage entries (`covEntry`, one per covered watcher, deduplicated: in `progressIfSync`
    the synced watchers on the channel, from the lock's map, not the stream's id map, which can
    repeat a watcher) and get them back; then `covFact` keeps the sender's `d`. (c) the earlier
    progress revisions at or below `p` (per watcher, a progress response's revision is the notified
    log's, which only grows: record its lower bound, `notifiedLb`, in `respCov`), and the start
    revision at or below `p` (the cache's watch starts at a revision etcd had reached). Then the
    client: `regFacts` keeps `createdAfter`; `mvccOk` says an announced watcher's responses before a
    response were all sent down (`SendInv.noPend`); the completeness part of `recvElem` and
    `cursorOk`; `serveSubstream` carries it; then `isEtcdWatcher_of_watcher`, `RequestProgress`, K3.
  - **K2e design analysis (2026-10-17)**. What the cache's
    `watchRespOk` needs beyond the client's `rangeWatchRespOk`, and what is missing:
    1. *Cursor semantics*: the client's cursor (`γ.cur`, `rangeWatchRespOk`'s `c'`) is the last
       event's revision, kept on an event-less response; the cache's moves to a progress
       response's revision. The client contract's consumers (recipes `waitEvents`, Election
       `observe`, leasing `waitRescind`/`monitorLease`, `waitDelete`) destructure
       `rangeWatchElem` (10 slots) and `rangeWatchRespOk` (2 slots, `Hsort.2.2`), so changing it
       ripples into them; a separate predicate and cursor avoids that.
    2. *Progress at `p` with the cursor `c ≤ p`*: needs that a progress response's revision is
       exactly the notified one (`progressIfSync` reads `rev()` under `s.mu.RLock`, and `End`
       notifies and commits in one `s.mu` critical section; the proof only knows the revision's
       log is a prefix of the notified one: `rev()` must take the lock body's committed-log
       fraction) and that a watcher's response revisions on the channel never decrease.
    3. *Event completeness*: derivable from `cursorOk`'s cumulative cut (`WatchContent.lean`
       `cut_step`, `watchEvents_mid`, v3rpc `WatchStep.lean` `srvStep_of_watch`), not exported by
       `dispatch_content`; exact cover (`rg.covers k ↔ pfx <+: k`) is needed (only covers ⇒
       inRange exists; `inRange_prefix` gives the prefix case).
    4. *Broadcast coverage*: `regFacts` must keep `createdAfter` and the `Created` snapshot
       (`run` drops them), and `mvccOk` must say every announced watcher's responses before a
       response were sent down before it (`SendInv.noPend`), for `covFact` to meet `cursorOk`.
    Then `isEtcdWatcher` from `isClientWatcher`, `RequestProgress`, K3.
- **K2 (the client: progress requests, completeness).** `RequestProgress` specified; `run` sends
  progress requests and broadcasts id `-1` responses (W-C's invariant: every substream in
  `substreams` has an open `recvc`, by K0); `rangeWatchRespOk` gains completeness (the events
  are the cut `watchEvents L rg a d` that `WatchContent.lean` already proves) and progress
  responses (nothing under the range changed up to the header revision), so the cache's
  `isEtcdWatcher` (its `watchChain` and progress case) follows; `isEtcdProgressNotifier` from
  `RequestProgress`'s spec.
- **K3 (the bundle).** `isEtcdClient` loses `isEtcdLeaseClient` (the cache never uses it; it would
  tie the cache to leases, unit T3); `isEtcdKVE`/`isEtcdTxnKV` at the server's instance (after
  `recipes/KVOfServer.lean`); `cache_end_to_end_client`.

## Unit C2a: a `Get` after a `Put` sees the `Put` (one server) (2026-10-14, branch `worktree-backend`)

Item 3 of the C2 plan below, at one member: a client's `Get` after its successful `Put` reads a
log that extends the `Put`'s. Design: `notes/decisions.md`, "A write's witness for later reads".

- **The witness** (`appliedWit γr log`, `InvRequest.lean`): `∃ i, committedAtLeast γr i ∗
  appliedLogAt γr i log ∗ appliedMono γr`: the log is the one applied through an index `i` the
  committed index has reached, and applied logs grow with the index (`appliedMono`, a capability
  read off the applied index's invariant: `appliedMono_of_inv`). A linearizable read at `i`
  (`readLogOk γr i l`: `l` extends the log applied through some `ci₀ ≥ i`) therefore reads `l`
  extending `log`.
- **The committed index past the entry** (raft as the code uses it, no new raft premise): the
  raft loop's `updateCommittedIndex(&ap, rh)` raises `s.committedIndex` to the batch's last index
  before `applyc <- ap`. `isReadyHandler rh R γr`'s `updateCommittedIndex` closure now gives
  `committedAtLeast γr v` (the server's closure: `setCommittedIndex`'s, or the writer half's lower
  bound when the index is already past `v`), `updateCommittedIndex.spec` gives `committedLast γr
  ce`, the `applyc` payload `rnApP` carries it, and `run` turns it into `batchCommittedIdx γr ce`
  (every entry's index is at most the last: `srvIdxOk`, `batchCommittedIdx_of_last`), a premise of
  `applyAll`, `applyEntries`, `apply` and `applyEntryNormal` (`committedAtLeast γr m.index`).
- **The deposit ahead** (`applied_predeposit`): the log after an entry is deposited in `γr.logs`
  at its index *before* its result goes to the waiter (`Trigger` in `applyEntryNormal`, or the
  NOSPACE alarm goroutine's), since the proposer may return before `setAppliedIndex`. A new ghost
  variable `γr.pend` (`ReadNames.pend`; halves in `srvAppliedInv` and the apply thread's
  `srvAppliedOwn`) says the next index's log is in (`srvAppliedPre γr v v' L`); `srvAppliedInv`
  allows the key `v + 1` then, and keeps the applied logs in prefix order (`appliedMonoMap`); the
  deposit needs the new log to extend the current one (the apply thread's `appliedLogAt γr v
  x.log`, and `entryStep_prefix`/`applyStep_prefix`/`chainStep_prefix`: a step only appends).
  `setAppliedIndex.spec` now takes `srvAppliedPre γr v v' L` (so `v' = v + 1`) and publishes it;
  `applyEntryNormal.spec` takes `srvAppliedOwn γr v ∗ appliedLogAt γr v x.log ∗ committedAtLeast
  γr m.index ∗ ⌜m.index = v + 1⌝` and returns `srvAppliedPre γr v m.index x'.log`; `apply.spec`
  takes `appliedLogAt γr (f0 - 1) x.log` and `batchCommittedIdx γr ms` (the loop invariant's
  `appliedLogAt` is now unconditional); conf changes deposit their (unchanged) log in `apply`.
- **The names** (`ReqNames.rd : ReadNames`): the wait's registration condition and results are
  stated at the request path's read names (`reqWaitR γi E γr`, `resultΨ E γr`, the new
  `resultIsW E γr` = `resultIs` with the witness, `waitInv` at `ρ.rd`); the apply thread's view
  `isServer … ρ γr` now says `ρ.rd = γr` (a pure conjunct), and the construction premise
  `isServerBuilt` has `"%Hρrd" ∷ ⌜ρ.rd = γr⌝` (what `NewServer` discharges by choosing the names).
- **Carried to the reply**: `processInternalRaftRequestOnce` returns `resultIsW E ρ.rd`,
  `raftRequest`'s `appliedOk E ρ.rd` has the witness, `EtcdServer.Put`'s success has `appliedWit
  ρ.rd x'.log`, `v3rpc.putAppliedOk s E ρ.rd` too (`put_end_to_end`), the client's `putReplyOk E
  γr` and `etcdPutSpec E γr` (`etcd_putHandlerOk` at `ρ.rd`; `etcd_kv_served` registers the `Put`
  at `ρ.rd`, the `Range` at `γr`: a user takes `γr := ρ.rd`).
- **The result** (`client/v3/Results.lean`): `client_get_after_put`: with `putReplyOk E γr
  (putKeyOp key val) cid mid mp` and `Range` registered with `etcdRangeSpec E γr`, `kv.Get(ctx,
  key)` returns `nil` and `m` with `getAfterPutOk E key val cid mid mp m` (the put's log after
  `x'.log = x.log ++ [put change]` a prefix of the get's certified `l`, `mp`'s revision ≤ `m`'s,
  the get's selection of `key` at `l`, and if no revision of `l` after the put's touches `key`,
  `m.kvs = [kv]` with `kv.key = key`, `kv.value = val`, `m.more = false`), or an error. Pure:
  `put_applied_log` (a successful put through any chain appended the client's put change),
  `get_after_put_kvs` (the corollary), `srvRangeOk_getKey`. `#print axioms` of
  `client_get_after_put`: exactly `client_get_end_to_end`'s and `client_put_end_to_end`'s (the
  axiomatized types and the gRPC trust boundary), no `sorryAx`; `get_after_put_kvs`: `propext`,
  `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`.
- **Statements changed** (strengthened, or premises the callers hold): `setAppliedIndex.spec`,
  `applyEntryNormal.spec`, `apply.spec`, `applyEntries.spec`, `applyAll.spec`,
  `updateCommittedIndex.spec`, `raftNode.start.spec` (`isReadyHandler … E.γr`),
  `processInternalRaftRequestOnce.spec`, `raftRequest.spec`, `EtcdServer.Put.spec` (stronger
  post), `request_delivered` and `applied_log_at` (restated with them), `put_end_to_end` (stronger
  post), the client's `putReplyOk`/`etcdPutSpec`/`etcdKVMethods`/`etcd_putMethodOk`/
  `client_put_end_to_end` (a read-names parameter, a stronger reply). No axiom, no `sorry`.
- **Left for C2**: the witness is one member's (`γr`, `E`); a cluster needs the committed index's
  cluster meaning (plan item 3 below) and one history. `DeleteRange`/`Txn` replies do not carry
  the witness yet (the same `appliedOk` has it; carrying it is the Put's change again).

## Unit P3b: the server end of the gRPC boundary (2026-10-14, branch `worktree-backend`)

The server side of the gRPC trust boundary moved below etcd's generated handlers, the quota
wrapper and the server's unary interceptors (design: `notes/decisions.md`, "The server end of the
gRPC boundary"), as unit P3a did on the client side.

- **grpc's server contract** (`Proof/google_golang_org/grpc/InvGrpc.lean`): `grpc.serve` (still
  one axiom for every service and method) now says that grpc's runtime runs, per call of a
  registered method, the `MethodDesc.Handler` of the registered `ServiceDesc` on the service value,
  with the call's context (`isContext`, `grpcRunCtx`), grpc's `dec` (`grpcDecOk`: decodes the
  request into the zero `*T` it is given, `ProtoMsg.recv`) and the interceptor grpc composes for
  the server's chain (`grpcSrvChain`, `srvChainWP`: `chainUnaryServerInterceptors`, as `chainWP` on
  the client); a run holds one of the `n` copies of `S`. The method's run contract is
  `grpcMethodOk mh srv ics S Spec`; `grpcListener addr` became `grpcServerAt addr ics regs`
  (opaque, exclusive: the server at `addr` built with the chain `ics`, the methods `regs` =
  `(full name, MethodDesc.Handler, service value)` registered; established by the unverified
  `v3rpc.Server`/`grpc.NewServer`/`Register*Server`/`Serve`). `isGrpcRpc` is now
  `∃ mh srv ics S, grpcServes … ∗ grpcMethodOk …`; the client side (`grpcInvokerOk`) is unchanged.
  `grpcHandlerOk` stays as the contract of a *service method* (below the interceptors). Also:
  `srvInterceptorOk ic R Q` (a transparent interceptor: calls the handler once on the same context
  and request and returns its result, or returns `(nil, err ≠ nil)`; `R` its per-run resource, `Q`
  what it reads of the request), `srvInterceptorsOk`, the theorem `srvChainWP_of_ok` (a chain of
  transparent interceptors), `grpcHandlerOk_frame`, `grpcDecOk_ty`.
- **Proved** (16 functions): the generated `_KV_Put_Handler`, `_KV_Range_Handler`,
  `_KV_DeleteRange_Handler`, `_KV_Txn_Handler` (`Spec|Proof/go_etcd_io/etcd/api/v3/etcdserverpb/`:
  for any messages of the method's Go types, any service value implementing `KVServer`, any chain
  of transparent interceptors); `NewQuotaKVServer`, `newBackendQuota`, `quotaAlarmer.check`,
  `quotaKVServer.Put` (`v3rpc/`: the quota check through the apply package's quota contract
  `apply.isQuota`, the NOSPACE alarm through `EtcdServer.Alarm`), the promoted
  `quotaKVServer.Range`/`DeleteRange` (method-set wrappers: `QuotaLemmas.lean`,
  `quotaKV_promotedHandlerOk`); `newUnaryInterceptor` (capability, learner, API-version and
  leader checks: each error path returns without the handler), `newLogUnaryInterceptor` (the
  handler, then `s.Logger()` and a deferred `logUnaryRequestStats`), `isRPCSupportedForLearner`.
  Vocabulary: `v3rpc/InvQuota.lean` (`quotaAlarmerAt`, `quotaKVServerAt`, `learnerReqOk`, the
  method-set class `QuotaKVServerIsKVServer`), `v3rpc/QuotaLemmas.lean`.
- **Restated** (`client/v3/Results.lean`): `etcd_putMethodOk`/`etcd_rangeMethodOk`/
  `etcd_deleteMethodOk` (`grpcMethodOk` of the generated handler on the `*quotaKVServer`, from
  the `kvServer` handlers' `grpcHandlerOk` through the quota wrapper); `etcd_kv_served` now takes
  `grpcServerAt addr [il, im, iu] regs` with the KV methods among `regs` (`etcdKVRegs q`), the
  quota wrapper over the `*kvServer` (`quotaKVServerAt`: `NewQuotaKVServer`'s post), the three
  interceptors' contracts (`newLogUnaryInterceptor`'s and `newUnaryInterceptor`'s posts;
  grpc-prometheus's, assumed), the method-set instance, and `N` slots of `etcdGrpcSlot`
  (`etcdRunSlot`, a `leadTimeMu` reader slot for the alarm, the log interceptor's `lgMu` slot);
  its conclusion is unchanged. `client_put_end_to_end`/`client_get_end_to_end` are unchanged.
- **New trust-boundary axioms**: `grpcServerAt` (opaque, replaces `grpcListener`);
  `EtcdServer.Alarm` (names-only: `raftRequest` of an alarm, with the request path's premises),
  `EtcdServer.IsMemberExist`, `EtcdServer.IsLearner` (the cluster's, names-only; `IsLearner`'s
  premise `membership.localKept c`, an axiomatized predicate: the local member stays in the
  members map, `issues/etcd-unary-interceptor-learner-removed.md`), `api.IsCapabilityEnabled`,
  `metadata.MD.Get` (grpc), `utf8.ValidString` (Go's `unicode/utf8`, names-only: new package),
  `prometheus.CounterVec.WithLabelValues`, `v3rpc.logUnaryRequestStats` (zap, peer, proto.Size,
  the stringers: it reads the request and the response, which the wire models trust read-only).
  Reused: `storage.NewBackendQuota` (the apply package's), `metadata.FromIncomingContext`.
  Package facts (v3rpc's `v3rpcInit`, `Base.lean`: `interceptorVars`): the five `rpctypes`
  errors returned, the three metadata keys, `clientRequests`. Method-set assumption:
  `QuotaKVServerIsKVServer` (a class, as context's `ErrorStringIsError`).
- **Translation**: `etcdserverpb.toml` (the four handlers, `RegisterKVServer`, `KV_ServiceDesc`,
  `KV_DeleteRange/Txn_FullMethodName`; `RegisterKVServer` translated, not proved: it needs a
  `RegisterService` contract and two method-set facts), `v3rpc.toml` (quota.go,
  `newUnaryInterceptor`, `newLogUnaryInterceptor`, `isRPCSupportedForLearner`; the promoted
  `quotaKVServer.Range`/`DeleteRange` must be listed for Goose to emit their wrappers), `api.toml`
  (`V3rpcCapability`), new names-only `unicode/utf8` (`etc/goose.py`). `goose.py --check` passes.
- **Links**: `etc/link-lean-first-v3rpc.txt` (the entries above; the server's getters `@`),
  `etc/link-lean-first-server.txt` (unit P4's list taken over); the v3rpc and server Links
  regenerated, the client's unchanged.
- **Gates**: full `lake build` green (4556 jobs); `goose.py --check` passes; `tcb-report.py
  --check` differs from the baseline (not updated): P3b's 11 axioms new (`grpcServerAt`,
  `EtcdServer.Alarm`/`IsMemberExist`/`IsLearner`, `membership.localKept` and its persistence,
  `api.IsCapabilityEnabled`, `metadata.MD.Get`, `utf8.ValidString`,
  `prometheus.CounterVec.WithLabelValues`, `v3rpc.logUnaryRequestStats`), `grpcListener` gone;
  P4's (`NewLoggableTxnRequest`, `RangeRequest.String`, `reflect.ValueOf` new; `InsertStep`,
  `WarnOfExpensiveReadOnly{Range,Txn}Request` gone). Collections `client`, `server`, `txn`,
  `v3rpc` differ likewise (the client results gain `EtcdServer.Alarm` and `grpcServerAt`: the
  interceptors' contracts are premises of `etcd_kv_served`). No `sorry`.
- **Not done**: `RegisterKVServer` (and `Server()`) unverified: the registration and the chain are
  the premise `grpcServerAt`; the interceptors' contracts in `etcd_kv_served` are those their
  constructors' proved specs return, not derived from a verified `Server()`; `quotaKVServer.Txn`
  translated, not proved (no `Txn` method spec registered); the metrics interceptor
  (grpc-prometheus) is a premise.

## Unit P3a: the client's retry interceptor proved, `rpctypes.Error` proved (2026-10-14, branch `worktree-backend`)

The gRPC trust boundary moved below etcd's client retry interceptor (design: `notes/decisions.md`,
"The retry interceptor proved: the gRPC boundary below it"), and `rpctypes.Error` (an axiom too
strong for its body, unit P1) is translated and proved.

- **grpc's contract, one level down** (`Proof/google_golang_org/grpc/InvGrpc.lean`,
  `Spec/google_golang_org/grpc/ClientConn__Invoke.lean`): `grpcConn conn addr ics dopts` (opaque,
  replaces `isGrpcConn`: the connection's unary interceptor chain and default call options);
  `grpcInvokerOk conn addr inv` (one attempt of grpc's `invoke`: a run of the handler served for
  a registered method, or a client error grpc's `status` accepts, the reply back owned,
  `ProtoMsg.own`; call options scalar or `grpc.Peer(p)`, `grpcOptOk`, whose buffers
  `grpcPeerBuf p` it writes); `chainWP` (the chain as `chainUnaryClientInterceptors` composes it).
  The axiom `grpc.ClientConn.Invoke.wp_proof` is now: `Invoke` is the chain over an invoker meeting
  `grpcInvokerOk`, with `combine(dopts, opts)`; still one axiom for every method.
- **The interceptor, proved** (`client/v3/Client__unaryClientInterceptor.lean`, the loop with its
  logging, short circuit, context errors, token refresh, safe-retry policy): it returns an
  `etcdInterceptorOk` closure (`InvKVConn.lean`: the old `Invoke` contract, taking the invoker);
  `isEtcdConn conn addr := ∃ ic, grpcConn conn addr [ic] [] ∗ etcdInterceptorOk ic` replaces
  `isGrpcConn` in `kvObjAt`/`clientKVAt` and the stubs' specs; the old `Invoke` statement is the
  theorem `etcdConn_Invoke` (`client/v3/EtcdInvoke.lean`). Also proved: `isContextError`,
  `Client.shouldRefreshToken`, `Client.refreshToken`, `isSafeRetry`, `isSafeRetryImmutableRPC`,
  `isSafeRetryMutableRPC`, `retryPolicy.String`, `filterCallOptions`, `reuseOrNewWithCallOptions`,
  `withMax`, `withBackoff`, `rpctypes.EtcdError.Code` (helpers `InvRetry.lean`: `optionsOk`,
  `retryOptsAt`, `optApplyOk`, `retryClientOk`, `clientErrOk`).
- **`rpctypes.Error`** (`api/v3/v3rpc/rpctypes/Error.lean`, with `ErrorDesc`, `EtcdError.Error`):
  premise `statusErrOk err` (`cache/v3/Base.lean`: `nil`, or a leaf error whose `Error()`,
  `GRPCStatus()` and `Is` return), result `statusErrOk err'`, `clientErr` kept; the package facts
  (`rpctypesInit`) gained `errStringToError`'s map (values `statusErrOk`), `EtcdError`'s method set
  (`rpctypesEtcdErrorTy`), the `EtcdError`s the interceptor compares with and
  `ErrGRPCNotSupportedForLearner` (a pointer). `status.FromError`'s spec (an axiom) had no premise
  (false: it calls `Error()`/`GRPCStatus()`): now `statusErrOk err`, with `Message()`; `status.Error`
  returns `statusErrOk`; callers adjusted: `ContextError` (premise and result `statusErrOk`),
  `ctxErrClient` (the context's errors `statusErrOk`), `putCallOut`/`rangeCallOut` (errors
  `statusErrOk`), `WatchResponse.Err` (premise `statusErrOk closeErr`), the watch contracts
  (`watchRespOk`: `statusErrOk` of the close error for `errStrOk`; `rangeWatchElem`: plus
  `statusErrOk` of it, `rangeWatchElem_closeErr`), leasing's `txnCommitResultO` (errors
  `statusErrOk`, for `acquire`'s `FromError`).
- **New trust-boundary axioms** (grpc, zap, names-only etcd functions): `grpc.Peer`,
  `peer.Peer.String`, `grpc.ClientConn.Target`, `status.Code`, `errors.IsStatusErr` (`errors.Is` of
  a status error against an `EtcdError` value or a pointer: Perennial's `wp_Is` needs a pointer

  `isGrpcConn`, `isGrpcConn_persistent`, `rpctypes.Error.wp_proof` (now a theorem).
- **Translation**: `rpctypes.toml` (bodies of `Error`, `ErrorDesc`, `EtcdError.Error`/`Code`; import
  of grpc's `status`), `client/v3.toml` (the interceptor's functions above; import of grpc's

  `peer.Peer`'s fields; `etc/goose.py`: packages `net`, `google.golang.org/grpc/peer`, lean root

- **Links**: `etc/link-lean-first-client.txt` (the interceptor's entries; `rpctypes_Error:

## Unit P2: the auth store's request side (2026-10-14, branch `worktree-backend`)

The real `authStore`'s request side is translated with bodies and proved
(`Proof/go_etcd_io/etcd/server/v3/auth/`): `IsAuthEnabled`, `Revision`, `isOpPermitted`,
`IsPutPermitted`, `IsRangePermitted`, `IsDeleteRangePermitted`, `IsAdminPermitted`,
`isRangeOpPermitted` and the permission cache's `checkKeyPoint`/`checkKeyInterval`/`isOpenEnded`,
`AuthInfoFromCtx` with `authInfoFromToken`; and `adt`'s `NewBytesAffinePoint`/
`NewBytesAffineInterval` (`pkg/v3/adt`). No `sorry`.

- **The invariant** (`auth.authInv st R`, `InvAuth.lean`): `revision`'s atomic in an invariant;
  `lg` (not nil), `be`, `tokenProvider` read-only with contracts (`authBackendOk be R`: the read
  transaction's `RLock`/`UnsafeGetUser`/`RUnlock` over the caller's read resource `R`;
  `tokenProviderOk`: `info` returns an auth info); `enabledMu` guarding `enabled`,
  `rangePermCacheMu` guarding the cache (every entry's two trees read-only, each with the
  contract `ivtQuery`: `Intersects`/`Contains` of a bytes-affine interval return). Readers hold
  `auth.authRd st R` (a slot of each `RWMutex` and `R`).
- **Derived** (`apply/AuthDerive.lean`, `etcdserver/AuthReqDerive.lean`):
  `apply.isAuthStorePerms_of_authInv` (the permission checks, `IsAdminPermitted`, `IsAuthEnabled`,
  `Revision`, with the reader resource `authRd st R`), `apply.authRevision_of_authInv`
  (`isAuthStore`'s `Revision` clause exactly), `isReqAuthR_of_authInv` (`isReqAuth` with the reader
  slot `enabledRd st` in its `AuthInfoFromCtx` clause; its `AuthInfoFromTLS` clause exactly).

- **Not derivable as stated: `isReqAuth`'s `AuthInfoFromCtx` clause and `isAuthStore`'s
  permission and `IsAuthEnabled` clauses** take no resource (`{{ True }}`), but the real methods

  (`NewBytesAffinePoint`'s `make([]byte, len(key)+1)`: unreachable in Go, but the model's `make`
  does not assume it). The R-forms add exactly these. Switching the server's premises to them is
  the next step: `isReqAuth` and `isAuthStore` gain a reader resource, threaded as the request

  request side (unit P2)").

  its value lists non-empty: narrower than grpc's code, true of grpc's transports;
  `issues/etcd-auth-token-md-empty.md`), `auth.authStore.AuthInfoFromTLS` (its peer's
  `credentials.TLSInfo` and x509 chains are axiomatized types; `issues/etcd-auth-tls-info-assert.md`),

  `simple_token.go`'s `info` locks its own mutex and reads a map; `jwt.go`'s parses a JWT with

  and `NewAuthStore` (not proved: it needs `refreshRangePermCache`, i.e. `getMergedPerms` building

  gains `Permission_Type` and its three constants; new `Code/google_golang_org/grpc/metadata.toml`
